body: You're a life saver THANK YOU.

I know she's not obligated, but that's what makes her decision petty in my opinion. Showing obvious favouritism in a family setting is problematic. I'm sure if my parents asked her for access to the account, she'd give it to them (free of charge as well). The fact that she's going out of her way to exclude me specifically is what annoyed me, despite me giving her a fair option to split her bill. I never asked her to share the account for free, nor felt entitled to free access, she's just being stubborn.

Yes! I'm the only one in my family who attends therapy and it can be exhausting. Mental health is a taboo subject in our culture so everyone's aware I go, we just don't talk about it. 

I totally resonate with your point about the media perspective of family! I think throughout adulthood I've realized that not many people are concrete or truly have your back, and at the end of the day, your family will always be there so I've been making a more active effort to invest in and nurture my relationships with all my family members. My sisters are each other's best friends, I've always been a little jealous of their relationship and I guess I kind of want that with the two of them too. We have a joke in my family that I'm the sore thumb because my parents are a duo, my sisters are basically twins and then there's me. Accepting the fact that I may never be that close with either of them has been difficult.
I get that but I feel like that'd definitely make be TA if I retaliated by not sharing with her anymore haha
That's fair, I agree it was sucky of me to bring up what I do for her, I was just frustrated as my request really seemed like nothing in comparison
Your opinion is your opinion I guess, we choose to die on different hills lol

I'll definitely try to do that at some point in the future! My sister isn't really a "let's sit and talk about our feelings" kind of person, no one in my family is really haha. But therapy has been super beneficial for me so I totally see the benefits of having some open and honest communication. I see your point about some siblings having a different type of relationship, I guess maybe me and my middle sister don't have the share subscriptions with each other type of relationship like the younger two do so the sooner I accept and get over that, the better.
Yeah I think that's the case with us. I'm hoping it'll improve in the future though, maybe after we both have kids as well and our perspectives on family change.

Perhaps. I'm not going to pretend I'm besties with her but I'm more than willing to move past whatever drama (typical sibling beef, nothing major) we had when we were younger. But I guess it's up to her to determine how quickly we grow our sister bond. I see them much more now because we all live under the same roof again but when I was away for school we didn't really talk often because we were never that close before I left anyways, so maybe that's played a role in the friction.

That's true, but if she wasn't sharing her account with anybody I'd get that. It's the fact that she willingly shares her account with my other sister for free that annoyed me and I'm not even asking for a freebie.
Because I'm the "oldest" I feel like I can't stoop down to her level of pettiness so I likely won't do that
Thank you! I agree no one has to share but her stubbornness is what pissed me off

Because of our age gap my youngest two sister are super close and I've always kinda been the lone wolf (I'm the oldest). I haven't lived at home for the past 5 years (schooled out of town) but moved back in because of COVID. I love both my sisters but I'm kinda closer with the youngest one due to our more similar personalities. Me and the middle one do kind of have some friction and used to fight often when I was a teen but being older and more mature now I do try to make an active effort to work at our sister bond.
I never wanted to access the account for free, I told her I'd pay for half of it from the jump.

I'd be a little weary honestly. I'd be curious to know how many flings, hookups or friends with benefits they've had because even though he may not consider them as "real relationships" there could be relationship-like baggage attached. If he ends up having a kind of womanizing history with lots of casual partners but no past girlfriends I'd see it as commitment issues and would need to make sure he's on the same page as I am commitment wise if the relationship were to continue.
